The claim petition has been filed by the petitioner against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.5,50,000/- with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 23.06.2024.
2.

The case of the petitioner in brief is as under:
That on 23.06.2024 at about 2.00 p.m., the petitioner was riding Hero Honda Passion Plus Motor cycle bearing Reg. No. KA-02-EL-2450 on left side of NH-48 Bengaluru - Tumkuru Road, near M.V.M. Kalyanamantapa, Kasaba Hobli,
Nelamangala Town, Bengaluru Rural District, at that SCCH-10 time, the driver of Tanker Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AF- 6691 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's Hero Honda motor cycle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the injured petitioner was shifted to Care Asia hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he took inpatient treatment.

He has spent more than Rs.80,000/- towards hospital charges, medicines, conveyance, nourishing food and attendant charges etc.
3. Further, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 71 years, he was doing coolie cum agricultural work and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
On account of the injuries sustained in the accident, he could not do his work, he became permanently disabled and put to irreparable loss of income.
Further, the alleged accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AF-6691.
The respondent No.1 being owner and respondent No.2 being SCCH-10 insurer of offending Tanker lorry
are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petition.
4. In pursuance to the notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Court, remained absent and placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before the Court through its counsel and filed the written statement.

5. The brief contentions of the respondent No.2 (insurer) are as under:

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending Tanker lorry contended that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case.

The respondent No.2 has denied the accident, the manner in which the accident took place, rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Tanker Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AF-6691 and its involvement in the alleged accident.

Further denied the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the alleged accident, treatment taken for those injuries, medical expenses incurred and permanent SCCH-10 disability suffered by him and also denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 has stated that, the respondent No.1 has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

Further contended that, as per the records the petitioner was aged more than 71 years and himself was solely responsible for the cause of alleged accident as he rode the motor cycle without wearing head guard in a zig zag manner, lost his control, without following any traffic rules and regulations, he himself dashed against alleged lorry from opposite direction.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
On these grounds, respondent No.2 prayed for dismissal of the petition against it.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that, on 23.06.2024 at about 2.00 p.m., while he was riding the Hero Honda Passion Motor cycle bearing Reg. No.KA-02-EL-2450 on the left side of NH-48 Bengaluru - Tumkuru Road, near MVM Kalyanamantappa,
Kasab Hobli, SCCH-10 Nelamangala Town, Bengaluru Rural District, at that time, the driver of the Tanker Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AF-6691 driven the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle, as a result, he fell down and sustained injuries ?
2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award?
7. The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW-1 and also examined two witnesses as PW-2 and PW-3 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
The respondents have not adduced any oral or documentary evidence on their behalf.
8. Heard the arguments.
Perused the materials available on record.

9. My findings to the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order, for the following :

The petitioner has filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.5,50,000/- with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident that took place on 23.06.2024.

sentences.text: To substantiate his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW-1 and also examined two witnesses as PW-2 and PW-3 and in all got marked documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.
Ex.P.1 is the copy of the FIR No.0271/2024 of Nelamangala Traffic PS and Ex.P.2 is the First information statement.

On perusal of Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2, it reveal that I.O. has registered a case against the driver of the Tanker lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AF-6691 for the commission of offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex.P.8 is the copy of charge sheet filed by the Nelamangala Traffic PS.

On perusal of Ex.P.8, it reveals that, after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against one Mr. Lava who is none other than the driver of offending Tanker lorry bearing Reg. No. KA-51-AF-6691 for the SCCH-10 offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
Further, as per wound certificate i.e. Ex.P.3 produced by petitioner and Ex.P.12 discharge summary, it appears that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident.

12. On perusal of the aforesaid documents, it is sufficient to conclude that the accident in question had taken place due to the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle and petitioner has sustained injuries in the said accident.

13. The respondent No.2 have seriously disputed the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and contended that, the petitioner himself solely responsible for the cause of alleged accident as he was riding the same in rash and negligent manner with high speed and dashed to the moving vehicle.

Though the respondent No.2 has contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligent riding of the petitioner and there is no SCCH-10 negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, they have not produced any contra documents to show that, the rider of the motor cycle has also contributed to the accident.
Further the police have not registered any case against the petitioner for his alleged negligent act.

14. As discussed supra, the IO after investigation has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending Lorry showing him as an accused in the said case and as per the police records, it reveal that the driver of the offending vehicle was driving the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and has caused the accident.
15. Besides, it is settled principles of law that, in a motor vehicles accident compensation cases strict proof of negligence is not required.

This view receives support from the law declared by Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009(13) SCC page 530 in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachalapradesh Road Transport Corporation and in AIR 2011 SC page 1504 in SCCH-10 the case of Parameshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others.

sentences.text: Thus, by considering the present facts of the case and the materials placed on record, I am of the opinion that, the accident in question had occurred due to the negligent and rash driving of the driver of the Tanker lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AF-6691.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
17. ISSUE No.2:-
This petition is filed for seeking compensation of Rs.5,50,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident.
As stated above, the petitioner has already proved that, the accident was occurred due to sole negligence on the part of driver of offending Tanker lorry.
The petitioner contended that, he has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
He further stated that, after the accident, he was shifted to Care Asia hospital, Nelamangala, wherein he took inpatient treatment.
SCCH-10 18

. Before proceeding to discuss this issue, I feel it necessary to reproduce the law declared by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2011(1) S.C.C page 343 in the case of Rajkumar Vs.
Ajay Kumar.
In para No.5 of the judgment, Hon'ble Apex Court has mentioned the heads under which compensation is to be awarded in personal injury cases.
I reproduce the same hereunder for convenience.
Future Medical expenses.
SCCH-10 Non-pecuniary damages (general damages) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
Loss of amenities (and / or loss of prospects of marriage) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).

sentences.text: Keeping in view the law declared in the aforementioned decision, I have carefully perused the entire materials placed on record.
The wound certificate of the petitioner has been marked as Ex.P.3.
As per the wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained fracture superior pubic ramus and doctor opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.
19. In this case, the petitioner has produced discharge summary as per Ex.P.12.

On perusal of Ex.P.12 it reveals that, the petitioner was admitted to the Care Asia hospital on 23.06.2024 and discharged on 24.06.2024.
20.
Ex.P.10 are the medical bills amounting to Rs.5,002/- and Ex.P.11 are the medical prescriptions.
The medical bills SCCH-10 produced by the petitioner appears to be genuine.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.5,000/- under the head of Medical expenses.
21. As per the medical documents it appear that, the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and he is suffering from physical disability.
By considering the nature of injury, the petitioner might have suffered pain and agony.
Considering the age of the petitioner, I am of the opinion that if Rs.30,000/- is awarded towards pain and sufferings it would be just.
If Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards nourishment and diet food it would be just.
22. The petitioner has contended that, before the accident he was hale and healthy and he was doing coolie and agricultural work and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/- per month.
It is further contended that, due to the injuries he is not able to do any work as he was doing earlier and also lost his income.
SCCH-10 23.
On behalf of the petitioner, the Doctor was examined as PW-2.
PW-2 in his evidence has deposed that, injured petitioner has sustained fracture of the right superior and inferior pubic ramus.

On recent examination, he has noticed that the petitioner has mild limping gait, restricted right hip joint movements and recent x-rays shows the united fracture. PW-2 doctor has assessed physical disability of the right lower limb at 47% and the whole body disability of the petitioner at 14%.
Though PW-2 doctor was cross-examined by the counsel for the respondent No.2, nothing was elicited from the mouth of the witness to disprove his evidence.
24. According to the petitioner, he was aged about 71 years at the time of accident and he was doing coolie and agricultural works and earning Rs.25,000/- per month.
To prove his age, the petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.9.
As per Ex.P.9, the date of birth of petitioner is shown as 15.08.1953.
The accident was occurred on 23.06.2024.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is considered as SCCH-10 71 years.
As per Sarla Varma's case the multiplier is applicable only up to the age of 70 years.

In the instant case, since the petitioner has crossed 70 years of age, this Court is of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future earning capacity due to permanent disability.

However, on perusal of the medical documents and evidence of PW-2 and the disability assessed by the doctor, it is crystal clear that, the petitioner Karivaradaiah vs Umesh K M on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147134287/
6 cannot do his normal work as he was doing earlier.

sentences.text: Hence, the disability of the petitioner will definitely come in the way of the petitioner in his day today activities.
Hence, considering the injuries suffered and the age of the petitioner, this Court is of the opinion that, due to disability, the petitioner must forego some comforts in his life.
Hence, I conclude that if Rs.50,000/- is awarded towards loss of amenities it would be just and proper.

25 . Thus, petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads;
SCCH-10 Sl.
 Heads Compensation No.
 1) Medical expenses Rs. 5,000 /-
 2) Pain and sufferings Rs. 30,000/-

3 ) Nourishment and diet food Rs. 5,000/-
 5) Loss of amenities Rs. 50,000/-
Total Rs.90,000/-
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.90,000/-.
26. REGARDING LIABILITY:
As discussed supra, this Court has arrived at the conclusion that, the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Tanker lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-51-AF-6691.
The respondent No.1 has insured the vehicle with respondent No.2, as such, respondent No.2 has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
Admittedly, the Insurance Policy was in force at the time of the accident.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the respondent No.1 RC owner of the vehicle and respondent No.2 insurer are jointly and severally SCCH-10 liable to satisfy the award.

The respondent No.2 being insurance company is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 has to pay the compensation of Rs.90,000/- along with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.
27. Issue No.3:

In view of my finding on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.90,000/- with simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of entire compensation awarded.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The respondent No.2 being insurer is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest within SCCH-10 30 days as contemplated under Sec.168(3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
